object_types.name: Patient
object_types.definition: A person who receives medical care at the clinic and books appointments.

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments.
Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: PatientId
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a patient, printed on their card.

source_references.excerpt: Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: Doctor
object_types.definition: A medical professional who examines patients and provides medical care during appointments.

source_references.excerpt: Each appointment is with exactly one doctor.
Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: LicenseNumber
object_types.definition: The unique license number that identifies a doctor.

source_references.excerpt: Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: Appointment
object_types.definition: A scheduled session where a patient meets with a doctor at the clinic.

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments.
Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: AppointmentNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for an appointment, assigned when the appointment is created.

source_references.excerpt: Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: ExamRoom
object_types.definition: A physical room in the clinic where appointments are conducted.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: RoomNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for an exam room.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: Specialty
object_types.definition: A medical specialty such as cardiology or general practice.

source_references.excerpt: Every doctor has exactly one specialty, like cardiology or general practice.

object_types.name: AppointmentDate
object_types.definition: The calendar date on which an appointment is scheduled.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

object_types.name: TimeSlot
object_types.definition: A fixed time slot (e.g., 09:00 or 09:30) at which an appointment is scheduled.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

object_types.name: AppointmentStatus
object_types.definition: The current state of an appointment.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment also has a status. The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled.

object_types.name: VisitReason
object_types.definition: The reason provided by the patient when booking an appointment.

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking.

object_types.name: FollowUpNote
object_types.definition: A note written by the doctor after an appointment describing follow-up care or observations.

source_references.excerpt: After the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note. At most one follow-up note per appointment.

ambiguities.description: Appointment scheduling uniqueness is unclear. The transcript states appointments are scheduled 'on a date and at a time slot' and that doctors 'see many patients', but it does not explicitly state whether a given date-time slot can accommodate multiple appointments or if each date-time combination is unique. Additionally, it is unspecified whether the uniqueness constraint applies per doctor or per appointment globally. For example, can two patients see two different doctors at the same date and time? Can one doctor have only one appointment per slot? This affects whether a composite uniqueness constraint should apply across Appointment, AppointmentDate, and TimeSlot.

Doctors see many patients across their appointments.

ambiguities.description: Visit reason and follow-up note optionality. The transcript uses 'can have' for both visit reason and follow-up note, indicating they are optional on the appointment side. However, it does not clarify whether every visit reason or follow-up note must be associated with some appointment, or if they can exist independently. This affects whether a mandatory constraint should apply on the value type side.

ambiguities.description: Exam room participation is unspecified. The transcript identifies exam rooms and mentions they have room numbers, but does not clarify whether appointments are held in exam rooms, or what the relationship is between appointments and rooms. Is every appointment held in exactly one room? Can a room host multiple appointments? This relationship may need to be added to the model.

ambiguities.description: Specialty value constraint. The transcript gives examples of specialties ('cardiology' and 'general practice') but does not explicitly state whether the set of specialties is restricted to a fixed list or is open-ended. If there is a controlled vocabulary of valid specialties, a value constraint should be applied to the Specialty value type.

ambiguities.description: Primary doctor must be a valid doctor. The transcript states 'every patient has exactly one primary doctor' but does not explicitly require that the primary doctor relationship resolves to an actual Doctor entity. It should be clarified whether the primary doctor assigned to a patient must exist as a registered doctor in the system (i.e., a mandatory referential integrity constraint).

source_references.excerpt: Yes, every patient has exactly one primary doctor. That's separate from who they happen to see in a given appointment.
